title: Constructing a singular reflected ray
reviewed_arguments: Smooth scalar second order, real principal symbol, arbitrary complex lower terms, noncharacteristic boundary and n at least two. The closed compressed arc has interior endpoints, injective positive-cosphere projection and locally finite transverse reflections.

The one-positive Gaussian seed has every negative Sobolev order but fails local L2. Empty Gaussian dimension is included. The actual seed proof, not a source citation, supplies its full wavefront and local critical threshold.

Both full ordered factorizations and exact two-sided Cauchy evolutions use the same complete initial profile. The right-root convention gives rho=lambda and tangential flow -H_lambda. The normal trace has elliptic principal gap 2 sqrt(R).

Joint kernel phases, both inverse graphs and the smooth parameter-dependent correction give the complete ambient wavefront. Tangential remainders act on its bounded-slope cone, so the original full differential equation is smooth. The normal extension theorem supplies the intrinsic jets.

S1 retains compact input and output graph supports, the smooth global Sobolev tail and every parameter derivative. Actual forced Duhamel and distributional adjoint/Schwartz uniqueness, including weighted moments, justify each incoming comparison.

Full canonical tubes remove every lower term after positive order reduction. The distributional primitive identifies the actual same transverse coefficient. Proper graph inverses continue it through caustics, retaining density and Maslov data.

At every subsequent reflection the complementary factor is elliptic on the incoming germ. The full incoming trace and forced uniqueness give agreement with exact evolution modulo smooth functions. Pairing the other root with the same datum gives exact zero trace and a nonzero outgoing singularity.

Compact positive-cosphere injectivity separates nonadjacent pieces despite possible intersections of their base projections. Reflection comparison handles collar overlaps. The finite chain therefore carries a single consistent microlocal distribution.

BGA1 constructs the full boundary-compatible left inverse. Tangential inversion keeps every normal derivative. Interior ordinary symbols are obtained only after a bounded-slope homogeneous angular cutoff; there the frequency weights are comparable. Exterior base multipliers give the exact left identity without an unaccounted commutator.

The actual N-domain smoothing lemma supplies one common collar for all normal jets. The complete operator partition has sum I to every order on the retained cones, exact tangential trace action near the boundary and cancellation of the full P commutators on overlaps.

Endpoint regularization uses one actually available finite negative Sobolev order M for an arbitrary continued compact profile. Each summand has simultaneous summable norm and every required Fourier derivative bound. Compact supports shrink to the endpoints; local finiteness and angular Fourier estimates prove the exact closed-ray wavefront.

Both endpoint forcing rays are necessary by the constant-model propagation theorem. BGA2 splices in canonical model time: the full derivative identity has a smooth transition defect and kills the auxiliary endpoint. Full conic gluing transfers it back without assuming injective base projection. Both patches are interior and preserve the boundary trace.

The main theorem has equality for both solution and forcing wavefronts, compact support in any prescribed neighborhood and exactly zero Dirichlet trace. Removing the base-velocity hypothesis uses uniqueness of the projected order-one Hamilton flow: an injective nonconstant orbit cannot hit a projected equilibrium.

The strip figure has three transverse contacts and two interior endpoints. Physical time and Hamilton orientation differ by s=-t/2. The compressed frame r(1-r) has the stated upper-wall sign; all four exact quadratic branches agree with the retained Bezier geometry.

All four complete solutions are retained. Flat trace and conormal signs, cubic mixed derivative scaling and Fourier gain, periodic distribution convergence and its unique positive wavefront, and all-real Gaussian Sobolev thresholds are checked. A3 adds both weight inequalities and the full elliptic argument proving local critical failure.
